message:
docs: clarify that maxParamLength does not prevent ReDoS (#7140)

Fixes #7082

The `maxParamLength` docs claimed the option protects regex routes
against ReDoS. It does not: in find-my-way 9.10.0,
`currentNode.regex.exec(param)` runs on the whole path segment
(everything up to the next `/`), and only the captured values are
compared against `maxParamLength` afterwards. With `maxParamLength: 10`
and `allowUnsafeRegex: true` on `/u/:id(^(a+)+$)`, an 11-char segment
takes about 10 ms, 27 chars about 357 ms and 29 chars about 1282 ms, all
ending in a 404. The actual ReDoS guard is the `safe-regex2` check
find-my-way runs at route registration, which is skipped only when
`allowUnsafeRegex` is `true`.

#### Changes

- The `maxParamLength` docs no longer claim ReDoS protection, explain
that the limit is checked against the captured values after the regex
has run on the full segment, and link to `allowUnsafeRegex`.

The code is unchanged: checking the length before `exec` would reject
segments that hold several regex params (e.g. `/:a(^\d+)-:b(^\d+)`)
whose combined length exceeds the limit while each captured value is
within it, so changing that is a find-my-way decision.
